note: Reference heights in pixels at 2x production scale. Validator check 4 ('size within ±15% of the category reference height', ASSET_PIPELINE §4.3 step 4) resolves an asset against this table. Every entry below is quoted from ASSET_PIPELINE §1.2 — nothing here was invented by the pipeline. A subject with no entry FAILS check 4 rather than passing silently: 'we do not know how tall this should be' is not a pass, it is an undeclared art decision. See `pending`.

modes.reference: Trimmed height must land within `tolerance` of `height`.
modes.envelope: Trimmed height must not exceed `height`. Used where §1.2 states the height of an ASSEMBLED subject but the asset is one part of it — a torso has no declared height of its own, but it cannot be taller than the adult it belongs to.

entries.reason: Character art is doll-rig parts assembled at run time. §1.2 gives the assembled adult, not the parts, so the only height fact available is that no part may exceed the whole.

entries.source: ASSET_PIPELINE §1.2 — Sedan araba = 90 px yükseklik, 288 px uzunluk (4.5 m)

entries.reason: Exceeds the 160 px split limit, so it exists only as `_lower` + `_upper`. The validator sums the pair before comparing against this height; neither half is checked against 200 on its own.

pending.note: Subjects in the stage 1–2 production set that ASSET_PIPELINE §1.2 does not give a height for. Each is an art decision that has not been made. They are listed rather than guessed, and any asset with one of these subjects fails validation until a height is added above with its source. Phase 4 generated no production art, so none of these blocked anything yet.
